chapter: Highlights, the reunion album and fellow musicians
title: Coleman Hawkins
summary: Coleman liked Paul Bascomb's solo on 'Lost in the Shuffle' and they became friends.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And, another thing I [Recording interruption] wanted to (inaudible) Coleman Hawkins or those that weren't exactly trumpet players.

I was getting ready to bring up Coleman Hawkins. Ben Webster. So, I was, I would say Ben Webster was one I really liked besides Coleman Hawkins. Coleman Hawkins used to do different concerts with the small group in Long Island. He was, I don't know. I forgot how they advertised. It said the "Hawks" or something like that.

And, when he first came back from Europe, Coleman Hawkins, that's when I first met him. He was over there about 12 years after I got to New York. And, he, Coleman Hawkins liked Paul Bascomb's solo on "Lost In The Shuffle". It was one of my records. And he came back, he came back to meet me. He said I want to meet that tenor man you've got on "Lost In The Shuffle". Paul liked Coleman and tried to play

somewhere on his style. And so they was, they liked each other, you know. And so, after that we got to be very close and friendly. And, we used to go out and go to a little jam session, hang out together. And Coleman, when we did a few, down to the small groups, we did a few concerts together.
